name: Forehand pendulum serve
summary: The most common serve. One swing, four spins: backspin, sidespin, no-spin and topspin.
whenToUse: As your main serve. Short backspin or no-spin stops attacks; long sidespin or topspin pushes your opponent back.

keyPoints.stance: Side-on in your backhand corner, left foot forward for right-handers (right foot if left-handed).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Turn the shoulders back as you toss, then turn forward through contact.
keyPoints.strokeLength: The bat swings like a pendulum from right to left (left to right if left-handed); the contact itself is short and fast.
keyPoints.timing: Contact as the ball falls, low, just above table height.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Close to the backhand corner, behind the end line.
keyPoints.freeArm: Flat, open palm; toss nearly straight up at least 16 cm, then move the arm out of the way.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow up and back, wrist cocked. Brush under the ball for backspin, around the side for sidespin, behind it for no-spin, up the back for topspin.
keyPoints.recovery: Step back into ready straight after contact.
keyPoints.anticipation: Plan the third ball: where will their return probably go?

cues: Legal toss: flat palm, 16 cm up
Brush where you want the spin

learningPath.task: Watch the toss and the swing at slow speed. Notice the contact point changes, the swing barely does.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: toss and swing without hitting, then with a ball in the air.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Was the ball on a flat, open palm?
Did it go up at least 16 cm, almost straight?
Did you hit it on the way down?

learningPath.task: Serve backspin; watch it stop or come back.
Serve all four spins, 5 of each.
learningPath.passCheck: 7 of 10 with the spin you meant.

learningPath.task: Short and long, mixed spins, to targets.
Serve and attack the third ball.
learningPath.passCheck: 6 of 10 third balls on the table.

learningPath.task: Test: serves in the target zone.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent loves to attack long serves.
gamePatterns.how: Serve short backspin or no-spin to their forehand, then attack the push.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent pushes every short serve back well.
gamePatterns.how: Mix in a fast long sidespin to their backhand or elbow.

fixes: Brush thinly, as if just grazing it

causes: Contact too high above the table
fixes: Let the ball drop near table height
Close the bat a little for no-spin and sidespin

causes: First bounce too far from the net
fixes: First bounce near the net on your side

troubleshooting.symptom: The umpire might call my toss
causes: Toss too low or thrown backward
fixes: Rest the ball on a flat palm
Toss nearly straight up, at least 16 cm

penholdNotes: Penholders serve with the same face and often get more wrist into the contact.
